people.name: Liam Horne
people.status: Leads product at Tempo, which launched the Machine Payments Protocol with Stripe in March 2026.
people.short: Co-built the Machine Payments Protocol at Tempo after leading OP Labs.
people.why: He connects a decade of Ethereum payments research with agents that finally need it. He started building on Ethereum in 2016, and in 2017 he and Jeff Coleman began work on state channels, publishing their Counterfactual design in 2018. He joined Optimism in February 2021 and became CEO of OP Labs in June 2022, steering the OP Stack. At Tempo, the stablecoin payments chain, he helped build the Machine Payments Protocol with Stripe, launched in March 2026 as an open standard built on HTTP 402. Software paying software, years early and right on time.

media.alt: Liam Horne's essay 'State Channels and Agentic Payments' on liamhorne.com
media.caption: State Channels and Agentic Payments — liamhorne.com/mpp

people.name: Steve Kaliski
people.role: Principal Software Engineer, Engineering Lead for Agentic Commerce
people.status: Engineering lead for agentic commerce at Stripe; co-author of the Payment HTTP authentication Internet-Draft (September 2026).
people.verifiedHow: Named as Stripe's engineering lead for agentic commerce on Stripe's ACP (Sept 2025) and MPP (Mar 2026) launch posts, and listed as a co-author of IETF draft-httpauth-payment-01.
people.short: Engineered Stripe's side of Instant Checkout and the Machine Payments Protocol.
people.why: He connects card issuing with checkouts no human clicks. He co-founded Bowery as CTO, then built at Beme and Frame.io before joining Stripe in November 2019, where he spent four years leading Issuing, the team behind Stripe's physical and virtual cards. In September 2025 he was engineering lead on the Agentic Commerce Protocol, developed with OpenAI to power Instant Checkout in ChatGPT, and in March 2026 he co-authored the Machine Payments Protocol with Tempo, now an IETF Internet-Draft. Cards first, then robots.

people.name: Brendan Ryan
people.status: Engineer at Tempo Labs; first author of the Payment HTTP authentication Internet-Draft, published September 2026.
people.verifiedHow: Listed as first author, Tempo Labs, on IETF draft-httpauth-payment-01 (Sept 9, 2026).
people.short: First author of the IETF draft that gives HTTP 402 real payment semantics.
people.why: He connects consumer apps, developer tools and stablecoins in the plumbing of machine payments. He built software at Pinterest, VSCO and GitHub, then at Stripe as an engineering lead, and at Bridge, the stablecoin platform. At Tempo Labs he is first author of draft-httpauth-payment, the IETF Internet-Draft published in September 2026 that turns HTTP 402 "Payment Required" into a standard payment challenge and underpins the Machine Payments Protocol. Reserved for decades, finally specified.

people.name: Aniket Das
people.status: At Meta Superintelligence Labs, where he built the team behind Muse, launched September 2026.
people.short: Built the engineering team behind Meta's Muse agent from scratch.
people.why: He connects augmented-reality effects with the first mass-market proactive agent. Across eight years at Meta he moved from AR and XR effects to leading the team that reimagined the Meta AI app. In early 2026 he was asked to drop everything for a new project at Meta Superintelligence Labs and built a team from scratch to make a truly personal assistant. It launched in September 2026 as Muse: an agent written in Rust that runs in its own virtual machine for each person, with guardrails and human-in-the-loop controls. A computer of its own, for everyone.

At Anthropic he created Claude Code on desktop, the app for running several coding-agent sessions side by side and reviewing their changes, and introduced its October 2026 update for parallel tasks. He announced his departure on October 23, 2026, promising to share what's next. He gave the terminal a window.

people.name: Soleio Cuervo
people.status: Hosts First of Kind, which launched Season 3 in October 2026; angel investor and design advisor.
people.verifiedHow: Facebook Like button design and Dropbox Head of Design role confirmed by PBS Frontline, TechCrunch (Dec 2012), New York Magazine (Apr 2018), and Design Buddies (Nov 2025); First of Kind Season 3 confirmed on firstofkind.com and YouTube.
people.short: Designed Facebook's Like button; former Dropbox Head of Design; hosts First of Kind.
people.signal: Facebook Like button → Dropbox → First of Kind
people.why: He connects the button billions of people tap every day with the founders and designers building for the agent era. After studying music composition and multimedia design at Duke, he joined Facebook in 2005 as its second product designer, spending six years shaping Notes, Video, Groups, Messenger and the 2009 News Feed redesign that introduced the Like button. In 2012 he joined Dropbox and became Head of Design, growing the team from three designers to nearly 40 and helping bring Mailbox and Readmill into the company. From 2014 to 2017 he advised Figma and backed it early, then co-founded the design-led seed fund Combine in 2016 and went on to angel-invest in Vercel, Framer, Cursor and Delphi. Today he hosts First of Kind, the design-and-technology series that launched Season 3 in October 2026 with Vercel founder Guillermo Rauch on the agentic web. One thumb up, then the whole frontier.

people.name: Alex Cornell
people.status: Leads design for Muse, Meta's personal AI agent launched in September 2026.
people.verifiedHow: Muse design leadership confirmed by Lenny's Newsletter and the How I AI podcast (Oct 2026).
people.short: Leads design on Meta's Muse agent; ex-Facebook Live, Cocoon, Linear.
people.why: He connects filmmaking, music and interface design with the first consumer agents. He apprenticed with designer Scott Hansen of ISO50, and in 2011 co-founded Firespotter Labs, the studio that became Dialpad; in 2012 he published the book Breakthrough with Princeton Architectural Press. He went on to lead design for Facebook Live, build Cocoon, which Substack acquired in 2021, and design the Linear mobile app. Back at Meta as a design director for generative AI, he leads design on Muse, launched in September 2026 to feel like messaging a friend, not using an AI app. Twenty-five million music plays, one agent.

people.name: Gretchen Röehrs
people.status: Senior Product Designer at Mercury, building personal banking.
people.short: Founding designer at Chime; designed Origin's AI advisor; now at Mercury.
people.why: She connects runway illustration, zero-to-one consumer fintech and AI-native money tools. After an internship on Vogue's web team, in 2015 she became the founding product designer at Chime, leading its product and brand design as the mobile bank scaled from 100 to 10 million accounts. From 2018 she spent five years as Senior Art Director at Rothy's, while Rizzoli published a collection of her fashion illustrations. She returned to early-stage product in 2023 as founding product designer at the AI shopping startup Listo, then in 2024 became Principal Product Designer at Origin, where she designed the conversational and proactive experience for its AI financial advisor. Today she designs personal banking at Mercury. Fine art to fintech, by hand.

people.name: Jeff Wu
people.status: Independent researcher since 2026, after alignment work at OpenAI (2018–24) and Anthropic (2024–26).
people.verifiedHow: Authorship confirmed on arXiv (InstructGPT, 2203.02155); career moves confirmed by New York Magazine (Oct 2026) and Turing Tree.
people.short: Second author of InstructGPT; now an independent alignment researcher.
people.why: He connects the instruction-following breakthrough with the open question of how labs govern themselves. He joined OpenAI in 2018 and in 2022 was second author of InstructGPT, the human-feedback training recipe that made ChatGPT possible, before working on models that critique their own outputs. In 2024 he moved to Anthropic as an alignment researcher, and in 2026 he left to work independently, explaining his choice in an October 2026 New York Magazine feature. He taught models to follow instructions; now he asks who sets them.

people.name: Tomek Korbak
people.status: Departed OpenAI in October 2026; co-wrote an open letter calling for clear rules on outside safety collaboration.
people.verifiedHow: Authorship confirmed on arXiv (2507.11473); OpenAI role confirmed by TechCrunch (Oct 8, 2026).
people.short: Co-first author of the chain-of-thought monitorability paper.
people.why: He connects cognitive science and philosophy with keeping AI agents honest. After a PhD at the University of Sussex on learning from human feedback, including time as a visiting researcher at NYU, he presented an oral at ICML 2023 on pretraining language models with human preferences. He worked on honesty training at Anthropic and on AI control and safety cases at the UK AI Security Institute, and in 2025 was co-first author of the cross-lab paper on chain-of-thought monitorability. At OpenAI he worked on monitoring agents for misalignment until October 2026. Reading the reasoning, so we can trust it.

people.name: Mikita Balesni
people.status: Departed OpenAI in October 2026; co-wrote an open letter calling for clear rules on outside safety collaboration.
people.verifiedHow: Authorship confirmed on arXiv (2507.11473); OpenAI role confirmed by TechCrunch (Oct 8, 2026).
people.short: Founding Apollo Research member; co-discovered the Reversal Curse.
people.why: He connects scheming evaluations with the race to keep AI reasoning readable. As a MATS scholar with Owain Evans he co-discovered the Reversal Curse, showing that models trained on "A is B" fail to learn "B is A." In 2023 he became a founding member of Apollo Research, building evaluations for scheming and situational awareness, and in 2025 was co-first author, with Tomek Korbak, of the cross-lab paper on chain-of-thought monitorability. He then joined OpenAI to work on alignment, until October 2026. He noticed the models noticing.

people.name: Jasmine Wang
people.status: Departed OpenAI in October 2026; co-wrote an open letter calling for clear rules on outside safety collaboration.
people.verifiedHow: Authorship confirmed on arXiv (2004.07213 and 2507.11473); OpenAI role confirmed by TechCrunch (Oct 8, 2026).
people.short: Co-led OpenAI's safety cases work after leading a UK AISI team.
people.why: She connects AI policy with hands-on safety engineering at the frontier. In 2019 she worked on OpenAI's policy research team and co-authored the 2020 report Toward Trustworthy AI Development. She went on to lead a team at the UK AI Security Institute focused on AI control, co-authored the 2025 chain-of-thought monitorability paper, and returned to OpenAI in 2025, where she co-led the safety cases program and coined "pacing" for matching deployment to safety evidence. She departed OpenAI in October 2026. Safety, at the right speed.

people.name: Manuka Stratta
people.status: Post-training researcher at OpenAI; helped shape the research direction for GPT-6 Intelligent UI (October 2026).
people.verifiedHow: OpenAI post-training role confirmed by TechCrunch (Mar 24, 2025).
people.short: Post-training researcher behind ChatGPT voice and Intelligent UI.
people.why: She connects self-driving perception and tech policy with models that know when to show, not tell. After a master's in computer science at Stanford, she worked on perception for autonomous vehicles and was a Presidential Fellow at the Center for the Study of the Presidency and Congress, researching secure 5G. At OpenAI she joined the ChatGPT team as a post-training researcher, and in March 2025 announced the Advanced Voice Mode update that stopped ChatGPT interrupting people mid-thought. In October 2026 she helped shape the research behind Intelligent UI, teaching GPT-6 when an interactive interface beats plain text. First it learned to pause; now it learns to draw.
